I've been dealing with depression for about 35 years, so I just keep waking up and will keep doing so until I don't. I know what I'm up against, as it has been against me for most of my life. I do not drink - I've tried beer and spirits and get nothing from it, besides intoxication, and that does not seem like a worthwhile goal. I do not smoke. I do not do drugs. Never have for either. So I do nothing, as the things I long ago gained some enjoyment or pleasure from have not had those effects since I was in my 20s. I pursue nothing. There is no passion for anything. I have a girlfriend because I have a girlfriend. I've talked with counselors, and whatnot, in the past. I've truthfully and openly answered anything they've asked, but I got really nothing from it, even after months, and so I do not bother anymore. If you care to know, I'm on Cymbalta and Wellbutrin. Of course, many people say you shouldn't take anti-depressants, and that I should instead plunge myself into exercise, being more social, going out more, eating better, etc. I think I shouldn't take them because they, as well as past cocktails , have done little to nothing. I could stop, but then I would also stop going to the Dr completely so as to avoid him over no longer taking them. For about the first 25 years of my life I just faked being normal and would cover things up just by being overly happy and joking and excited about things, always acting like nothing was ever wrong. An unhappy childhood trained me well for that role. But by my 30s I was over it and just decided it was easier to no longer go out and around others and as friends moved away and moved on, I chose to not develop new friendships and to just soak in my own feelings of worthlessness without having to put on a happy appearance and attitude. The nagging reality was always there in my head to remind me anyway, so I just decided to let it have its way and since no once was much around to see these changes anyway, I could stop pretending and just deal with myself, on my own, and feel no embarrassment or pity from others. I've been staying home and in bed at least 3 days a month instead of going to work. I will usually just text my boss that I am not feeling well, or that I could not sleep (both of which are actually true, often) and once the pressure of having to go to work that day is released, I can then sleep, and sleep I do, usually for a full 24 hrs or more, skipping that missed workday completely by remaining in bed until the following morning, where I do get up and go in. Seems like I often do this on a Tuesday. I feel guilty about that, of course, but really I suppose it's more embarrassment and disappointment in myself than guilt.
